messages:
alex: seeing a weird fallback ordering at the edge during the 11:00 spike — tenant A got routed to the tiny quant model before the medium q2. logs show capacity on medium was reported available but then CB fired?

sam: can you paste the raw route headers the proxy sent to the gateway? could be a header precedence bug (x-rw-fallback-priority vs x-rw-fallback-hint).

alex: here: `x-rw-fallback-hint: prefer-medium,avoid-small` and `x-rw-fallback-priority: small,medium,large` — looks contradictory, gateway picked `priority` but capacity calc used `hint` for preemptive routing.

maria: urgh that conflict is exactly the problem. we defined semantics as: explicit `priority` wins, `hint` is advisory for routing prefetch/cache. but proxy may be merging these incorrectly.

priya: quick thought — we should short-circuit when circuit-breaker metadata says capacity estimates are stale. otherwise the router tries to schedule into a lane that just tripped a CB and immediately rejects, causing the chain to advance to the smallest model. that matches what you saw.

sam: agree. proposal: change router evaluation order to: 1) validate circuit-breaker and lane health 2) apply explicit `priority` header 3) apply `hint` for cost-sensitive substitutions 4) fallback chain evaluation. this avoids cycling into already-tripped lanes.

alex: sounds good. what about quotas? Tenant A was over quota for medium but had burst credits — the gateway dropped into small instead of deferring to burst pool.

maria: we're missing a `quota-defer` phase in the decision graph. flow should be: capacity check -> quota check -> quota-defer (if enabled) -> fallback. Right now quota check is terminal.

priya: implementation detail: add a `defer_window_ms` per-route (default 100ms) where requests can wait for burst credits or inflight batch completions. That keeps p95 latency bounded while reducing unnecessary fallback.

sam: example route config snippet:
```
route: /api/chat
backend: edge-proxy
fallback_chain: ["gpt-medium-q2", "gpt-small-int8", "gpt-tiny-int4"]
priority_header: x-rw-fallback-priority
hint_header: x-rw-fallback-hint
quota_defer: { enabled: true, defer_window_ms: 100 }
circuit_breaker: { error_rate_threshold: "0.04", cooloff_ms: 120000 }
```

alex: :thumbsup: that config would have kept tenant A on medium. two followups: 1) telemetry — we need events for every decision (capacity-skip, cb-tripped, quota-deferred, fallback-used) 2) console UX — show fallback chain visualization per route and per rollout so SREs can debug why a request hit a smaller model.

maria: on telemetry we already emit `fallback_used` but it's just a counter. propose richer dims: `origin_header`, `final_model`, `decision_path` array (e.g., ["capacity_ok","quota_blocked","quota_deferred","fallback_applied"]). makes alerting and trial analysis easier.

priya: Rollout UX: add a toggle to show the active fallback chain in the rollout diff. When you flip a canary, show predicted capacity impact and estimated cost delta if canary triggers fallback more often.

sam: we should also rate-limit re-routing churn. add a short TTL on per-request routing hints so repeated retries don't oscillate between lanes. maybe attach `x-rw-routing-epoch` header and ignore hints if epoch changed within 30s.

alex: one more edge case: cross-region fallback. If primary region is full but cheaper region has capacity, we prefer local fallback models then cross-region as last resort. need a flag `allow_cross_region_fallback` per-tenant. otherwise latency spikes.

maria: agreed. default false. ops can opt-in per contract. add telemetry for cross-region-fallback_lat_ms too.

deploy-bot: deploy started: routing/fallback-fix v2 -> staging at 1828654400 by @sam

sam: deploying a small change that flips evaluation order and adds quota-defer hook. will monitor fallback_used and cb_tripped metrics in console.

priya: i'll add an alert on sudden jump in `final_model == gpt-tiny-int4` rate. if it crosses 2% of traffic in 5m window, page SRE.

alex: thanks all. follow-up: @maria can you open a tiny RFC for the header precedence semantics and include the TTL/epoch idea? once we agree we'll roll to prod with a canary.

maria: on it — I'll draft and link to this thread.

sam: LGTM. monitoring hooks in console should include a per-route decision flamegraph for the last 1k requests — makes root cause way easier.

alex: that would have saved us 15mins debugging today :sweat_smile:
